messages:
arun: FYI ran a cross-cloud throughput sweep for the A100 (same sku) to investigate strange capacity sizing numbers. results look like a crossing curve rather than a constant delta between providers. attaching quick notes below.

maria: interesting, crossing curve how? like aws faster at low batch, gcp at high?

arun: exactly. with seq=128, bs=1-4, AWS p95 is ~28ms, GCP ~34ms. but at bs>=8 GCP throughput exceeds AWS by ~12%. suspect kernel launch / small-batch overhead differences due to driver or kernel selection.

jonathan: did you keep CUDA & driver consistent? any firmware/pcie differences?

arun: kept model binary identical, but drivers differ: AWS nodes shipped driver 525.89 + CUDA 11.8; GCP had 535.54 + CUDA 12.1; Azure was 535.65 on a different microcode. Also CPU affinity differs (AWS CPUs pinned to numa0, GCP had default interleaved).

sophia: can you paste the run command and the perf snippet?

arun: run command: `./run_bench.sh --model llama-13b-q8 --seq 128 --batch-sizes 1,2,4,8,16 --cuda ${CUDA} --driver ${DRIVER} --reps 30 --profile launch_latency`

arun: sample output (trimmed):
```
provider | bs | tokens/s | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | gpu_util
AWS      | 1  | 420      | 28.2    | 42.7    | 52%
GCP      | 1  | 360      | 34.1    | 51.3    | 48%
Azure    | 1  | 390      | 31.0    | 46.0    | 50%
...\nAWS      | 16 | 6400     | 210.4   | 310.7   | 88%
GCP      | 16 | 7200     | 185.1   | 278.2   | 92%
Azure    | 16 | 6950     | 192.0   | 285.9   | 90%
```
`launch_latency` is a custom histogram of kernel launch -> first token emitted.

maria: that pattern screams "launch latency tail". small batches dominated by kernel dispatch overheads and CPU->GPU submission path. different driver+cuda combos optimize that differently.

jonathan: did you try forcing CUTLASS vs cuBLAS kernels? we saw similar cross-over when fallback to cuBLAS for matmul sizes < 512.

arun: yes. forced CUTLASS via env `USE_CUTLASS=1` and reran. GCP improved for bs<=4 by ~10%, AWS stayed similar. looks like GCP's CUDA 12 runtime picks a CUTLASS path that has lower per-launch overhead for our tiling.

sophia: queue depth / submission batching on CPU side might mask this. how about coalescing 2 requests on CPU side?

arun: tried `--cpu-coalesce=2` (coalesce micro-batches) — AWS gained ~8% at bs=2 but lost a few % at bs>=8 (higher latency due to serialization). GCP saw smaller improvement because it already had lower launch latency.

infra-bot: deploy note: AWS has GPU driver package updated to 525.116 in next image build (ETA 2 days) — will test on rollout.

jonathan: did you inspect kernel-level timings? nvprof/nvtx traces?

arun: grabbed nvprof traces and plotted kernel_launch_hist for seq_len=128, bs=1. GCP shows a tight peak at 120-150us, AWS a wider spread 140-400us with a long tail. p99 aligns with that tail. I can drop the hist PNG into the benchmark bucket.

maria: good. that long tail explains capacity planning difference: p95 used for SLA sizing will favor AWS for small-batch latency, but throughput-driven autoscale should prefer GCP for bulk processing. we need to surface both in Console.

sophia: also check syscalls: `ioctl` latency spikes were correlated on AWS in one trace — could be kernel driver interactions with MKS (microcode?).

arun: noted. filed infra ticket with traces: https://redwood-internal/gists/bench-2065432100

jonathan: recommendation?

arun: for now: 1) pin driver+cuda per fleet for consistent SLOs 2) add a small-batch perf profile in model onboarding (seq<=256, bs<=4) that records launch_latency histogram 3) autoscaler should consider provider-specific throughput curves when suggesting capacity (avoid single-slope linear extrapolation).

maria: also add a note to Optimize: try `--warm-coalesce` (pre-warm a mini-batch to populate kernels/KV cache) — reduces launch tail on AWS by ~15% in my quick test.

jonathan: can we capture these as a short runbook? I'll draft one and drop into eng-ml runbooks.

bench-bot: snapshot created: s3://bench-exports/2065432100/ (configs, nvprof traces, histograms, run_log.txt) :white_check_mark:

arun: thanks all. putting these results into the onboarding checklist so QE sees it before we flip quantization flags.

sophia: nice work — this is exactly the weird cross-cloud case we needed to document.

maria: tagging @ops to watch drift when infra updates drivers. :eyes:
